title_en: Supreme People's Court Publishes Typical Cases of Drug Crimes and Serious Crimes Induced by Drug Abuse
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Typical Cases of Drug Crimes and Serious Crimes Induced by Drug Abuse Published

Case 1

Liu Fucheng et al. v. — trafficking and transporting drugs

——Organized AIDS patients to transport drugs multiple times, used minors to traffic drugs multiple times, extremely serious crimes

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant: Liu Fucheng, male, Han nationality, born on January 4, 1969, farmer.

From December 2001 to January 2007, the defendant Liu Fucheng, alone or jointly with others, organized several persons (most of whom were AIDS patients) to go to Mangshi City and Ruili City in Yunnan Province, and used methods such as body concealment to transport heroin to Zhengzhou City in Henan Province, Guangzhou City in Guangdong Province, and other places on 9 occasions, each time transporting between 50 grams and 976 grams of heroin, totaling 2,666.62 grams of heroin.

From July 2005 to April 2008, the defendant Liu Fucheng trafficked heroin in Guangzhou City: once 92.1 grams to Tong Weiming (sentenced in a separate case), once 10 grams to Wang Jinhua (separately handled), and in Zhengzhou City, trafficked heroin 10 times totaling 889.7 grams to Su Xijing (co-defendant, sentenced to life imprisonment), totaling 12 times and 991.8 grams of heroin trafficked. Among these, Liu Fucheng directly traded heroin with drug buyers on 4 occasions, and instructed others to trade with drug buyers on 8 occasions (of which 3 occasions involved instructing the same minor to trade with drug buyers).

In summary, the defendant Liu Fucheng, alone or jointly with others, trafficked and transported heroin on 21 occasions totaling 3,658.42 grams. After his arrest, Liu Fucheng reported the criminal acts of others who trafficked and transported 296 grams of heroin, which was verified.

(II) Judgment

This case was tried at first instance by the Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province and at second instance by the Henan High People's Court. The Supreme People's Lawfully conducted a death penalty review of the case of defendant Liu Fucheng for trafficking and transporting drugs.

The court held that the defendant Liu Fucheng, knowing it was a drug, trafficked and transported it, and his conduct constituted the crime of trafficking and transporting drugs. Liu Fucheng trafficked and transported drugs with high frequency and large quantities, causing great social harm. Liu Fucheng played a major role in the joint crime, was the principal offender, and had circumstances such as organizing AIDS patients to transport drugs and using minors to traffic drugs, with extremely serious crimes, and should be punished heavily according to law. After his arrest, Liu Fucheng reported the major criminal acts of others, which was verified, constituting major meritorious performance. However, Liu Fucheng's crimes were extremely serious, and his merits were insufficient to offset his crimes, so he was not given a lenient punishment according to law. Accordingly, Liu Fucheng was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved according to law.

The criminal, Liu Fucheng, was executed on March 31, 2012 in accordance with the law.

Case 2

Hu Biaowu v. — trafficking drugs

——Had been sentenced to a severe punishment for drug trafficking, trafficked drugs again after completion of the punishment, extremely serious crimes

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant: Hu Biaowu, male, Hui nationality, born on February 1, 1947, farmer. On March 9, 1992, he was sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve for the crime of drug trafficking; he was paroled on October 13, 2007, and the parole supervision period expired on December 12, 2009.

On December 29, 2010, the defendant Hu Biaowu purchased 2 pieces of heroin in Weishan Yi and Hui Autonomous County, Yunnan Province, intending to traffic them in Wuzhong City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. The next day, Hu Biaowu carried the purchased heroin and took a long-distance bus from Xiaguan Town, Dali City, Yunnan Province. When the bus arrived at the Nanhua Toll Station on Nanyong Highway in Nanhua County, Yunnan Province, public security officers seized 700 grams of heroin from Hu Biaowu's travel bag in the luggage compartment.

(II) Judgment

This case was tried at first instance by the Chuxiong Yi Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court of Yunnan Province and at second instance by the Yunnan High People's Court. The Supreme People's Court lawfully conducted a death penalty review of the case of defendant Hu Biaowu for drug trafficking.

The court held that the defendant Hu Biaowu, knowing it was a drug, trafficked it, and his conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Hu Biaowu trafficked a large quantity of drugs, causing great social harm, with extremely serious crimes. He had previously been sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve for drug trafficking, and within five years after the completion of that punishment, he again committed the crime of drug trafficking, constituting a recidivist and a repeat drug offender, with deep subjective malice and high personal danger, and should be punished heavily according to law. Accordingly, Hu Biaowu was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved according to law.

The criminal, Hu Biaowu, was executed on June 20, 2012 in accordance with the law.

Case 3

Li Yaqiong v. — intentional homicide

——After taking drugs, developed a mistaken belief, stabbed one person to death with a knife, extremely serious crimes

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant: Li Yaqiong, female, Han nationality, born on December 8, 1986, nightclub waitress.

At about 5:00 a.m. on December 31, 2009, the defendant Li Yaqiong, after taking ketamine, called and sent messages to her friend Lin Wei (male). Lin did not reply. Li then contacted her colleague Hua Lihua (victim, female, died at age 21) and learned that Hua was drinking with others in a bar private room in Jiangcheng District, Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province. Li Yaqiong suspected that Hua Lihua was with Lin Wei and believed that Hua intended to seduce Lin, so she formed the intention to kill Hua. Li Yaqiong carried a kitchen knife to the bar private room where Hua was, tricked Hua into the restroom, and struck Hua more than 100 times on the head, shoulders, arms, etc., causing Hua to die from acute hemorrhagic shock. After committing the crime, Li Yaqiong cut her own left wrist with the kitchen knife and was later apprehended by public security officers.

(II) Judgment

This case was tried at first instance by the Yangjiang Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province and at second instance by the Guangdong High People's Court. The Supreme People's Court lawfully conducted a death penalty review of the case of defendant Li Yaqiong for intentional homicide.

The court held that the defendant Li Yaqiong intentionally and unlawfully deprived another person of life, and her conduct constituted the crime of intentional homicide. After taking drugs, Li Yaqiong mistakenly believed that the victim was seducing her friend, struck the victim more than 100 times with a kitchen knife, causing death on the spot. The criminal circumstances were vile, the means were extremely cruel, the crimes were extremely serious, and she should be punished according to law. Accordingly, Li Yaqiong was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved according to law.

The criminal, Li Yaqiong, was executed on June 21, 2012 in accordance with the law.

Case 4

Wang Xiaoqing et al. v. — illegal trading of precursor chemicals

——Refined precursor chemicals from ephedrine compound preparations and then trafficked them, convicted and punished for the crime of illegal trading of precursor chemicals

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant: Wang Xiaoqing, male, Han nationality, born on July 2, 1965, farmer. On September 30, 2003, he was sentenced to six months' imprisonment for the crime of illegal business operation.

Defendant: Yang Pingxian, male, Han nationality, born on March 17, 1966, unemployed.

Defendant: Wang Qixiang, male, Han nationality, born on February 4, 1974, farmer.

Defendant: Zhang Peng, male, Han nationality, born on January 23, 1965, farmer.

Defendant: Wang Yilin, male, Han nationality, born on August 10, 1962, farmer.

Defendant: Zeng Hongbao, male, Han nationality, born on March 18, 1982, farmer.

Defendant: Liu Linquan, male, Han nationality, born on June 11, 1967, farmer.

Defendant: Liu Linhui, male, Han nationality, born on July 23, 1963, farmer.

In April 2009, the defendant Yang Pingxian, for the purpose of trafficking ephedrine for profit, rented an abandoned factory in Shuangliu County, Sichuan Province, and hired the defendants Zeng Hongbao, Liu Linquan, Liu Linhui and others to refine ephedrine using illegally purchased "compound theophylline ephedrine tablets." On March 9, 2010, Yang Pingxian instructed Zeng Hongbao to sell 200 kilograms of refined ephedrine to the defendant Wang Xiaoqing. On March 12 of the same month, public security officers seized a batch of production equipment and reagents from the above processing plant, and from a water tank in the plant seized liquid containing ephedrine components, and also seized more than 28.38 kilograms of ephedrine from Yang Pingxian's office.

From January to March 2010, the defendant Wang Xiaoqing repeatedly purchased ephedrine from the defendant Yang Pingxian and others, and then on 4 occasions organized or jointly with the defendants Wang Qixiang, Zhang Peng, Wang Yilin and others drove to transport a total of more than 475 kilograms of ephedrine from Sichuan Province to Guangdong Province for sale to others.

(II) Judgment

This case was tried at first instance by the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province and at second instance by the Sichuan High People's Court.

The court held that the defendants Wang Xiaoqing, Wang Qixiang, Zhang Peng, and Wang Yilin illegally traded the state-controlled precursor chemical ephedrine; the defendants Yang Pingxian and Zeng Hongbao illegally manufactured ephedrine and trafficked it for profit; the defendants Liu Linquan and Liu Linhui, knowing others were trafficking ephedrine, produced it for them; their conduct all constituted the crime of illegal trading of precursor chemicals. Wang Xiaoqing illegally purchased ephedrine and then repeatedly organized others and personally participated in trafficking, with large quantities. In the joint crime, he played an organizing and directing role, being the principal offender, and should be punished for all his organized, directed, and participated crimes. Wang Qixiang, Zhang Peng, and Wang Yilin illegally traded a large quantity of ephedrine, all participated under instruction, played secondary roles in the joint crime, being accomplices, and should be given lenient punishment according to law. Yang Pingxian hired others to manufacture and traffic ephedrine, with large quantities. In the joint crime, he played an organizing and directing role, being the principal offender, and should be punished for all his organized and directed crimes. Zeng Hongbao, Liu Linquan, and Liu Linhui were employed to participate in the manufacture or trafficking of ephedrine, with large quantities. In the joint crime, they all played secondary roles, being accomplices, and after arrest truthfully confessed their crimes, so they were all given mitigated punishment according to law. Accordingly, the defendant Wang Xiaoqing was sentenced to ten years' imprisonment; the defendant Yang Pingxian was sentenced to eight years and six months' imprisonment; the defendant Wang Qixiang was sentenced to seven years' imprisonment; the defendant Wang Yilin was sentenced to six years' imprisonment; the defendants Zhang Peng and Zeng Hongbao were each sentenced to five years' imprisonment; the defendant Liu Linquan was sentenced to three years and six months' imprisonment; the defendant Liu Linhui was sentenced to three years' imprisonment.

The above judgment became legally effective on June 20, 2012.

Case 5

Xi Hailong et al. v. — trafficking and manufacturing drugs

——Refined precursor chemicals from ephedrine compound preparations and then manufactured drugs, convicted and punished for the crime of manufacturing drugs

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant: Xi Hailong, male, Han nationality, born on November 14, 1976, unemployed.

Defendant: Liang Sibing, male, Mongolian nationality, born on November 23, 1982, unemployed.

Defendant: Wang Peng, male, Han nationality, born on April 12, 1989, worker.

In July and August of 2011, the defendant Xi Hailong learned from the defendant Wang Peng, through online chatting, phone calls, etc., the method of using "New Contac Capsules" to refine pseudoephedrine and manufacture methamphetamine. In September of the same year, Xi Hailong conspired with the defendant Liang Sibing to manufacture methamphetamine for trafficking and profit. Liang Sibing funded the purchase of the drug-manufacturing "New Contac Capsules" and arranged drug sales channels; Xi Hailong funded the purchase of other raw materials and equipment and was responsible for the specific manufacturing. Later, Xi Hailong refined pseudoephedrine from "New Contac Capsules" in rented houses in Hohhot City and Chifeng City of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region and manufactured 47 grams of methamphetamine. Through Liang Sibing's arrangement, Xi Hailong sold 15 grams of that methamphetamine to others.

(II) Judgment

This case was tried by the Hongshan District People's Court of Chifeng City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

The court held that the defendants Xi Hailong and Liang Sibing manufactured drugs and then trafficked them, and their conduct constituted the crime of trafficking and manufacturing drugs. The defendant Wang Peng taught others the method of manufacturing drugs, and his conduct constituted the crime of imparting criminal methods. Xi Hailong and Liang Sibing jointly manufactured 47 grams of methamphetamine and sold 15 grams of it to others, trafficking and manufacturing a relatively large quantity of drugs, and should both be punished according to law. After arrest, Xi Hailong truthfully confessed his crimes and assisted in the capture of Wang Peng, showing meritorious performance, so he was given a lenient punishment according to law. After arrest, Liang Sibing and Wang Peng truthfully confessed their crimes, so they were both given lenient punishment according to law. Accordingly, the defendants Xi Hailong and Liang Sibing were each sentenced to thirteen years' imprisonment; the defendant Wang Peng was sentenced to three years' imprisonment.

The above judgment became legally effective on May 7, 2012.

Case 6

Chen Xudong et al. v. — trafficking and manufacturing drugs

——Knowing others were manufacturing drugs using ephedrine compound preparations, provided assistance, deemed joint offender of the crime of manufacturing drugs

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant: Chen Xudong, male, Han nationality, born on February 20, 1972, unemployed.

Defendant: Liu Qiulin, male, Han nationality, born on August 2, 1972, farmer. On February 2, 1996, he was sentenced to seven years' imprisonment for the crime of theft.

Defendant: Zhou Chunhong, female, Han nationality, born on March 27, 1990, farmer.

From September 2010 to February 2011, the defendant Chen Xudong manufactured methamphetamine in a rented house in Luogang District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, and successively recruited the defendants Liu Qiulin and Zhou Chunhong to participate jointly. Chen Xudong funded and instructed Liu Qiulin to purchase the drug-manufacturing "New Contac Capsules" and other raw materials and equipment, agreed to share profits after the matter was accomplished, instructed Zhou Chunhong to remove the capsule packaging, paid Zhou compensation and promised to build a house for Zhou in her hometown after obtaining profits. Chen Xudong himself used the above pharmaceuticals to refine pseudoephedrine and manufacture methamphetamine. On February 22, 2011, public security officers seized from the above rented house tablets containing methamphetamine components (47.6 grams), liquid (5,585 grams), capsules containing pseudoephedrine components (1,167 grams), tablets (2,460 grams), liquid and solid-liquid mixture (3,289 grams), and other drug-making raw materials and tools.

From November 2010 to February 2011, the defendant Chen Xudong on 4 occasions sold a total of 273 grams of methamphetamine and 1,100 "Magu" pills (a type of methamphetamine tablet) to others. On February 22, 2011, public security officers seized from Chen Xudong's car white crystals containing methamphetamine components (10.88 grams) and red tablets (1.05 grams).

(II) Judgment

This case was tried at first instance by the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province and at second instance by the Guangdong High People's Court.

The court held that the defendant Chen Xudong, knowing it was a drug, trafficked it, and jointly with others manufactured drugs, and his conduct constituted the crime of trafficking and manufacturing drugs. The defendants Liu Qiulin and Zhou Chunhong jointly with others manufactured drugs, and their conduct constituted the crime of manufacturing drugs. Chen Xudong trafficked and manufactured a large quantity of drugs. In the joint drug-manufacturing crime, he played an organizing and directing role and was mainly responsible for the drug-making operations, being the principal offender, and should be punished for all his organized, directed, and participated crimes. Liu Qiulin and Zhou Chunhong participated in manufacturing a large quantity of drugs, knowing others were manufacturing drugs and providing assistance, playing secondary roles in the joint crime, being accomplices, and after arrest truthfully confessed their crimes, so they were both given mitigated punishment according to law. Accordingly, the defendant Chen Xudong was sentenced to life imprisonment; the defendant Liu Qiulin was sentenced to ten years' imprisonment; the defendant Zhou Chunhong was sentenced to three years' imprisonment.

The above judgment became legally effective on June 18, 2012.
